messages.subject: Re: Read.Model (Extract)
messages.body_plain:
Hi J.D.,

I think you need what=c("summaries", "parameters") so that what is a vector of things to extract. At the moment, "parameters" is being interpreted by R as the recursive argument of readModels since you're passing it as an additional argument.

Michael

messages.subject: Error extracting MODEL RESULTS in output file:
messages.subject_clean: Error extracting MODEL RESULTS in output file:
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am trying to read mplus output files using MplusAutomation package. I have done this so many times before. When I try to extract the item difficulty parameters from the output file, I get the following error:

> iter=101;main1<-readModels(paste("mplus",iter,".out",sep=""))$parameters$irt.parameterization$est[ 12:21]
Reading model:  mplus101.out
Error extracting MODEL RESULTS in output file: mplus101.out
<simpleError in names(parsedParams) <- columnNames: 'names' attribute [5] must be the same length as the vector [2]>

I am attaching the output files that I used with the following R code:

library(MplusAutomation)
iter=101;main1<-readModels(paste("mplus",iter,".out",sep=""))$parameters$irt.parameterization$est[ 12:21]

do you have any idea about this error?

Best,
Sedat

Hi,

First, I'm very thankful to have this R package - so thanks for your work on this!

I'm doing an LCA (with 4 classes) with distal outcomes. Because my reference class is Class 3, the main output section that MplusAutomation returns

I'm wondering if anyone has any recommendations on how to scrape the output for the other section:

I'd be ok with either of the following sections:
--ALTERNATIVE PARAMETERIZATIONS FOR THE CATEGORICAL LATENT VARIABLE REGRESSION
--ODDS RATIO FOR THE ALTERNATIVE PARAMETERIZATIONS FOR THE CATEGORICAL LATENT VARIABLE REGRESSION
--CONFIDENCE INTERVALS FOR THE ALTERNATIVE PARAMETERIZATIONS FOR THE CATEGORICAL LATENT VARIABLE REGRESSION

both of which have subsections like "Parameterization using Reference Class 1" etc.

Attaching my output file in case that's helpful.
Thanks!
Kim
